    Parse the GROBID XML output of a citation list

    parse_citation_list.Rd

    Parses the TEI XML returned by the GROBID processCitationList service used with grobid_process_file() or directly via process_citation_file() and transforms it into a structured tibble, with one row per parsed citation. Optionally allows attaching the raw original citation strings to the extracted metadata.

    Usage

    parse_citation_list(xml_content, raw_references = NULL)

    Arguments

    xml_content

    A character string containing raw TEI XML, a path to an XML file, or an xml2::xml_document object, as returned by grobid_process_file() with service = "processCitationList".

    raw_references

    An optional character vector containing the raw citation strings submitted to GROBID, in the same order as the <biblStruct> nodes of xml_content. If provided and its length does not match the number of parsed citations, a warning() is issued and raw_reference is set to NA for unmatched entries. Default NULL.

    Value

    A tibble with one row per parsed citation and the following columns: ref_n (integer, position of the citation in the entry), raw_reference (original citation string, or NA), title, authors (character, concatenated "Last name, First name" pairs), authors_list (list-column of data frames with first_name / last_name), year (integer), journal, publisher, volume, issue, pages, doi, pmid, url, ref_type (character, inferred reference type), and parse_confidence (numeric, from the GROBID confidence attribute, NA if absent). If no citation is found in xml_content, a zero-row tibble with the same schema is returned and a message is displayed.

    See also

    process_citation_file(), parse_references(), parse_header(), parse_fulltext()

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Typical usage via the high-level wrapper
txt_file <- system.file("extdata", package = "CheckrefR") |>
  list.files(pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  (\(x) x[1])()
citations_xml <- process_citation_file(txt_file, output_format = "raw")
parse_citation_list(citations_xml)
} # }

# Direct usage on a raw TEI XML fragment
xml <- paste0(
  "<TEI xmlns='http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0'>",
  "<text><body><listBibl>",
  "<biblStruct confidence='0.9'>",
  "<analytic><title level='a'>A sample title</title></analytic>",
  "</biblStruct>",
  "</listBibl></body></text></TEI>"
)
parse_citation_list(xml)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 16
#>   ref_n raw_reference title  authors authors_list  year journal publisher volume
#>   <int> <chr>         <chr>  <chr>   <list>       <int> <chr>   <chr>     <chr> 
#> 1     1 NA            A sam… NA      <NULL>          NA NA      NA        NA    
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: issue <chr>, pages <chr>, doi <chr>, pmid <chr>,
#> #   url <chr>, ref_type <chr>, parse_confidence <dbl>
